note: The Serbian Nemanjić dynasty and the Bulgarian tsardom competed for Balkan hegemony and Byzantine succession throughout the 13th–14th centuries. Stefan Nemanja allied with the Bulgarians against Byzantium; his successors alternately competed and cooperated with Bulgaria. Stefan Dušan's conquest of much of Bulgaria's western Macedonian territories (1330s) as part of his Balkan empire-building directly weakened Bulgaria before the Ottoman advance. The Bulgarian-Serbian competition prevented Balkan Christian unity and created the fragmented political landscape that the Ottomans exploited.

_quarry.structural_significance: The Nemanjić-Asen dynasty rivalry is one of the primary reasons for Balkan Christian disunity against the Ottoman advance; the competition for Macedonia (the most strategic Balkan territory) exhausts both powers simultaneously; both Bulgaria and Serbia collapse within decades of each other, creating the Ottoman opportunity
